title: runtime: add KV-cache hit-rate instrumentation + standardize SCM metric tags (with backfill)
author: Omar El-Sayed
description: Context: Standard Cost Model (SCM) needs cache effectiveness signals (KV-cache hit rate / savings) that are explainable and comparable across Hosted/Dedicated/Private. Today we have partial counters and inconsistent tag sets across runtime emitters, which makes attribution brittle and forces the Cost Model service to guess. This PR adds first-class KV-cache hit-rate instrumentation in the serving runtime and standardizes the tag set used for SCM-relevant metrics. It also implements explicit backfill behavior when tags are missing (rolling restarts, older clients, or partial deployment metadata), so we avoid dropping series while still making “assumptions” auditable. Changes: (1) Add KV-cache lookup counters and derived hit-rate gauge: - counters: runtime_kv_cache_lookups_total{result=hit|miss|bypass}, runtime_kv_cache_prefill_tokens_total, runtime_kv_cache_prefill_tokens_cached, runtime_kv_cache_bytes_cached_total - gauge: runtime_kv_cache_hit_rate (computed in-process as hit / (hit+miss), excluded from alerting until enough traffic) (2) Standardize SCM tag set across runtime metrics emitted by router + model runner: required: deployment_mode, region, gpu_sku, model_id, model_version, quant_profile_id, scm_route_id, tenant_tier; optional: dedicated_pool_id (Dedicated only), vpc_id_hash (Private only) (3) Tagging backfill strategy: - region: if missing, backfill from node label runtime.node_region; if still missing, emit region="unknown" and tag_missing="region" - gpu_sku: backfill from node label runtime.gpu_sku; else gpu_sku="unknown" + tag_missing="gpu_sku" - quant_profile_id: backfill from model runner config (resolved at model load); else quant_profile_id="default" + tag_assumed="quant_profile_id" - scm_route_id: if request has no route binding (legacy callers), emit scm_route_id="unattributed" + tag_assumed="scm_route_id" Note: we intentionally do NOT backfill model_id/model_version; those are required at the runner boundary and missing is treated as a bug (drops metric with runtime log + counter runtime_metric_dropped_total{reason="missing_model_id"}). (4) Cardinality controls: ensure scm_route_id is the normalized internal route identifier (NOT raw URL path), and tenant is represented as tenant_tier only (no tenant_id). Adds linting guardrails to prevent accidentally tagging with request_id/session_id. (5) Perf/overhead: counters use per-request aggregation + periodic flush; no per-token increments. Added microbench + on-host perf sampling (see notes below). Testing/validation: - unit tests for tag normalization + backfill behavior (table-driven) - integration test in runtime harness for KV-cache hit-rate sanity (hit rate increases after warmup on fixed prompt set) - added “canary-only” metric for early validation: runtime_kv_cache_hit_rate_canary{...} gated behind feature flag runtime.metrics.enable_kv_cache_hit_rate_canary Rollout: behind feature flag runtime.metrics.enable_scm_cache_signals (default OFF). Telemetry pipeline work to ingest/aggregate these series is in ENG-23155 / PR #18519; until then, these metrics are visible only in local / staging Prometheus. Perf notes: on A100 runner, p50 request overhead <0.3% CPU; on L4 runner, <0.6% CPU; no measurable latency regression in decode path (we avoid touching inner token loop). Follow-ups: - add server-side derived metric in metrics pipeline (preferred) once series are stable, and deprecate in-process gauge - update Cost Model service to consume runtime_kv_cache_prefill_tokens_cached/total and report cache_savings_tokens + confidence when tag_missing/tag_assumed present - align docs on required tag set (docs PR forthcoming)
commits: runtime/metrics: add kv-cache lookup + prefill token counters
runtime/metrics: standardize SCM metric tag set + normalization helpers
runtime/metrics: implement tag backfill + tag_missing/tag_assumed markers
runtime/tests: add table-driven tests for tag normalization and backfill
runtime/perf: add microbench + sampling notes for metrics overhead
runtime/config: add feature flags for scm cache signals + canary gauge
conversation: Logan Wright (review): Love the direction. Two asks: (1) please ensure we never emit tenant_id as a tag (even hashed), and (2) can we standardize on `scm_route_id` vs `route_id` across emitters? Right now I see both in the PR description and code.

Omar El-Sayed (author): Good catch. Updated emitters to use scm_route_id everywhere (normalized internal route id). Added compile-time guard in scm_tags.go to reject tenant_id / tenant / org_id tags. Also updated docs/internal/telemetry/scm_metric_tagging.md to explicitly call this out.

Thomas Baird (review): Backfill behavior: region="unknown" is fine, but please add a separate label indicating missing vs unknown-by-design. Otherwise downstream can’t tell if it's a bug or a real “unknown region” (which shouldn't exist).

Omar El-Sayed (author): Added `tag_missing` and `tag_assumed` labels (single value, not a boolean per field to avoid exploding cardinality). When multiple fields are missing we pick highest priority missing field (region > gpu_sku > scm_route_id > quant_profile_id) and increment runtime_tag_backfill_total{field=...}. Added tests.

Nadia Rahman (review): For token counters: can you confirm these are request-level aggregates and not per-token increments? We’ve been burned by hot paths before. Also, name suggestion: prefer `_total` suffix only for counters; gauge should be `_ratio` or similar.

Omar El-Sayed (author): Confirmed: we update a small struct during request lifecycle and flush once at end-of-request; no per-token increments. Renamed gauge to runtime_kv_cache_hit_ratio and kept runtime_kv_cache_hit_rate as an alias for one release (both behind flag) to avoid churn in early dashboards.

Sofia Ivanova (review): Please ensure `result=bypass` increments when caching is disabled by policy (e.g., sequence length too long / memory pressure). That’s important for SCM explain output (cache not used vs cache missed).

Omar El-Sayed (author): Implemented bypass classification. For now: bypass when kv_cache_enabled=false OR cache policy rejects (max_seq_len, memory_pressure, incompatible_quant). Added enum mapping and a unit test that bypass + miss are mutually exclusive per lookup attempt.

Jordan Lee (review): Determinism note: SCM expects consistent semantics. Can you document whether hit ratio is computed over lookups or over tokens? PR description mentions both. Also, how do we treat partial hits?

Omar El-Sayed (author): Clarified: hit/miss counters are per lookup decision; token counters are for prefill tokens reused (cached) vs total prefill tokens. Partial hits count as hit for lookup counter but token counters capture the actual reused portion. Updated doc and comments in kv_cache_metrics.go.

Logan Wright (review): LGTM once you remove the in-process gauge from default emission; I’d prefer we keep only counters and let pipeline compute ratios. If you need a gauge for local debugging, gate it tightly.

Omar El-Sayed (author): Done. Gauge is now behind runtime.metrics.enable_kv_cache_hit_rate_canary and only emitted in staging/prod-canary environments (env gate + flag). Mainline emission is counters only.
release_notes: Adds KV-cache effectiveness signals (lookups hit/miss/bypass + prefill token reuse counters) and standardizes SCM telemetry tags with explicit backfill markers; gated behind runtime.metrics.enable_scm_cache_signals.
